A frame from the previous clip may remain visible briefly during the next segment. Clamp emitted frame durations to segment boundaries; the remaining risk is narrow.
Security architecture risk: Low · up to 3159f
The checked export paths preserve redaction before framing and isolate retry attempts in separate output sessions. No introduced security bypass was established, but exceptional error delivery and cleanup remain partly unverified. **Retained concerns** No architecture-level concerns identified.
Security review details
**Security Blast Radius** - _inferred_ — The traced exposure is the selected local recording, supplied scene assets, and newly created export sessions. Preset fields change rendering and encoding policy without adding source-access credentials or a new privileged destination in this path. **Trust Boundaries and Controls** - _inferred_ — The suspected framing privacy bypass is not supported: neither Fill cropping nor blurred padding reads the original frame outside the redaction compositor. This conclusion concerns composition order, not independent authorization of renderer-supplied content or runtime pixel validation. **Resilience and Maintainability Implications** - _observed_ — Expected export failures are caught and returned as identity-guarded worker messages. Native worker.onerror lacks that guard and invokes failure handling through mutable current-session references. This handler predates the PR; whether a terminated attempt can deliver such an error during retry remains unresolved. Abort rejection is also ignored by the pre-existing teardown path. **Hardening Proposals** - _proposed_ — Apply the same attempt-identity check to every worker-originated terminal callback, including native errors, so retry isolation does not depend on post-termination event-delivery behavior.
